papers.title: Architecting Conversational Data Systems for Stateless LLM APIs: The Hydration Proxy Pattern
papers.innovation: Proposes the 'Hydration Proxy Pattern' to address the architectural gap created by stateless LLM APIs in conversational systems. This pattern enables client applications to manage conversational state and semantic context efficiently, thereby bridging the statelessness of LLMs with stateful application needs.
papers.benchmarks: The paper identifies an 'architectural gap' as the problem. While no specific named benchmark is provided, the innovation aims to solve challenges related to 'horizontal scalability' and 'managing the entire burden of conversational state and semantic context'.
papers.use_case: Essential for AI engineers building and deploying scalable, robust, and state-aware conversational AI applications using stateless LLM APIs, by providing a practical architectural solution for offloading and managing conversational state.

papers.title: Belief-Calibrated Optimization: An Explicit World Model for Agentic Optimization
papers.innovation: Introduces 'Belief-Calibrated Optimization,' a method that uses a coding agent as an optimizer to iteratively refine and improve the scaffold around a frozen LLM agent. The coding agent reads current scores and traces, then edits the source code to produce new candidates in an optimization loop.
papers.benchmarks: The abstract mentions using 'current scores and traces' for iterative improvement. No specific named benchmark suite is detailed, but the core objective is to improve the performance and effectiveness of LLM agents through this optimization process.
papers.use_case: Highly relevant for AI engineers focused on optimizing the performance and reliability of LLM agents, enhancing agentic workflows, and systematically improving prompt engineering and agent scaffolding through an iterative, code-based approach.

papers.title: The Memory Trust Gap: Capability-Dependent Failures in Persistent-Memory Agents
papers.innovation: Identifies and analyzes the 'memory trust gap,' a critical failure mode in personalized AI agents where stale stored facts in persistent memory can override current authoritative evidence without warning. The research studies how this harm evolves as model capability changes.
papers.benchmarks: Evaluates this phenomenon using a 'frozen, closed-set, action-scored benchmark with 2 suites' designed to represent different meanings of evidence interpretation.
papers.use_case: Crucial for AI engineers designing and developing robust and trustworthy AI agents that rely on persistent memory. It provides insights into mitigating risks associated with stale or outdated information and ensuring proper, reliable integration of current evidence.
